items.title: Thanksgiving Will Be Chilly And Rainy In Chicago, But Snow Unlikely
items.description: After an unusually warm stretch, temperatures are expected to stay in the 40s through Thanksgiving.

items.title: Metra Adds Another Holiday Train After Tickets Sold Out ‘In Minutes’
items.description: The new train is scheduled for Dec. 20 on the Metra Electric Line, with $10 tickets going on sale at noon Monday.

items.title: City’s Largest Tent Encampment In Uptown Park Sparks Calls From Neighbors To Assist Unhoused
items.description: The area near the lakefront in Edgewater and Uptown has the highest concentration of tents in the city, and it’s only grown over the past year, neighbors said.

items.title: After Drama Over Sky Ride Tap’s Iconic Sign, Owner Says He’s Keeping It
items.description: After the sign was removed and speculation swirled online sparked by a Chicago Sign Museum Instagram post, owner Kyriakos “Carl” Damianides said he has no plans to sell it.

items.title: Here’s Where 1st Video Gambling Machines Went Live In Chicago — And Where They’re Coming Next
items.description: Longtime Loop restaurant Miller's Pub is among eight Chicago businesses now operating video gambling terminals. They are among 100 already approved by the state.

items.title: Christkindlmarket’s Famously Stinky Raclette Cheese Sandwich Is Back: ‘Just Give It A Try’
items.description: The pungent raclette sandwich from Baked Cheese Haus drew first-timers and fans on the market's opening day. It's “not for everybody,” said cheesemaker Joe Burns.

items.title: Shop Local 2026: A Chicago Food Gift Guide
items.description: Make the holidays a little sweeter for your foodie friends and family with these Chicago-flavored treats.

items.title: How A Group Of Apartment Investors In Chicago Led To Financial Ruin And Street-Level Blight
items.description: Investors were responsible for nearly 40 percent of large apartment foreclosures citywide, an investigation has found.
